extracted.intended_audience: editors, proofreaders, authors, typographers, and publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Comprehensive copyediting and typographic guidance for preparing manuscripts and printed works, covering punctuation, capitalization, hyphenation, typography, references, tables, and proofs. Intended to standardize form and mechanize editorial decisions across publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colon: definition and rules for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the colon and gives rules and illustrations for its uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use after salutatory phrases in letters; between place of publication and publisher's name; with introductory remarks of a speaker; to emphasize close connection between clauses; to introduce statements, extracts, etc.; to separate chapter and verse in Scripture passages; to introduce clause from illustration or amplification; for hours and minutes in time-indications (pp. 131-136).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comma: definition and comprehensive rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition, illustrations, and an extended set of rules governing comma use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules cover omission between two adjectives, use after signatures and authors' names, use after digits indicating thousands, before 'and/or/nor', before 'of' with residence/position, omission between consecutive pages, comma with adjectival/adverbial/antithetical/appositional/parenthetical/participial clauses, to indicate omissions, to separate identical or similar words, to separate numbers and proper nouns, and other specific contexts (pp. 141-162).

rubrics_metrics.name: Semicolon: uses and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustration and rules for semicolon usage, including separation in complex lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare with comma usage; place semicolons to mark division of sentence; use in enumerations and to separate Scripture passage segments containing chapters (pp. 137-140).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation marks: rules for use and punctuation placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules for using quotation marks and interaction with other punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When to omit quotation marks for reduced citations; handling of colon, comma, ellipsis, exclamation point, interrogation point, and period in relation to quotation marks; use of single vs double quotes; special rules for Preface/Index, etc. (pp. 74-91, 136, 162, 181, 128-130, 126).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashes (em, en, other): definitions and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines dash types and gives rules for their uses and sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains em-dash and en-dash, different sizes; uses include indicating break/stop/transition/change, emphasis, to precede summarizing clauses, to connect numbers, to denote pause/implication, for emphasis in literary references, and in connection with parenthetical and complementary clauses (pp. 166-175, 258-263).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphens and Hyphenization: rules and compound formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of hyphens in compounds, for division, and hyphen leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers hyphen use in compounds (co-, pre-, re-, semi-, demi-, quasi-, non-, over-, under-, by-, vice-, ex-, etc.), hyphenated word division avoidance, number of consecutive hyphens at line ends, indicating omitted elements, and when to hyphenate fractions and syllable division (pp. 182-214, 210, 213).

rubrics_metrics.name: Italics: definition and rules for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines italics and enumerates contexts where italics are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for emphasis, titles of books/works, foreign words/phrases, names of genera/species, letters designating unknown quantities, some addressing lines, words to be emphasized, initial words 'Resolved', symbols for subdivisions, titles/positions after signatures, and continuation words (pp. 58-73, 60-72, 254).

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods (full stops): placement and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for period placement and exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes placing periods with quotation marks, omission after headlines, after initials of titles of publications, after MS, after certain abbreviations, omission after linguistic epoch abbreviations, and standard end-of-sentence rules (pp. 122-126, 123, 125).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipses: rules and treatment within quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for ellipsis usage and treatment as part of quotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for use of ellipses to indicate omissions; treat ellipses as part of quotation; page references for detailed rules (pp. 180-181, 88).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclamation point: rules for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when and how to use the exclamation point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for outcry and emphasis; interaction rules with quotation marks; also used for ironical words/phrases (pp. 127-128, 77).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogation point (question mark): rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use interrogation points for direct questions and queries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct questions followed by interrogation points; indirect questions not followed by interrogation point; use for 'Query' and special placement rules with quotation marks (pp. 129-130).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parentheses and Parenthetical clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for parentheses, including use for interpolations, explanations, and parenthetical clauses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for use of parentheses with parenthetical clauses (cf. dashes and commas); placing periods inside parentheses; using brackets within parentheses; numbering/letters for subdivisions (pp. 176-178, 126).

rubrics_metrics.name: Brackets: use for explanations and interpolations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of brackets for editorial explanations and to indicate omissions/interpolations inside parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brackets to indicate interpolations, explanations, or omitted words within quoted material (pp. 178).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers, Figures, and Numerals: rules for presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for when to spell out numbers vs set in figures and how to punctuate groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell out numbers commencing sentences; treat groups of six or more closely connected digits in figures; round numbers treatment; use comma after thousands; use comma to separate numbers; use dash for 'to' connecting ranges; Roman/Arabic numerals spacing at beginning of lines/headlines; use of commas between consecutive pages (pp. 94-98, 159, 173, 271).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates: formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format dates in publications and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates of publication to follow volume numbers in periodical references; omit st/nd/rd/th from dates; use comma between month and year when needed (pp. 237, 102, 160).

rubrics_metrics.name: References and Literary References: punctuation and abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for formatting references, punctuation, and standard abbreviations in bibliographies/literary references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes list of words to be abbreviated, punctuation of references, use of dash in connection with references, abbreviated periodical citation conventions like 'Ibid.' and 'Op. cit.' and special handling of Scripture/classical references (pp. 232-238, 174, 236).

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles of works and headings: capitalization and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for capitalization of principal words in titles and whether to italicize or roman-quote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize principal words in titles of publications, essays, plays, poems, pamphlets, periodicals; rules when to italicize, roman-quote, or use roman-quotation marks; treatment of 'The' in newspaper titles; treatment of subdivisions and serial titles (pp. 41, 60-83, 43, 80-82).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization: general rules and many categorical applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for capitalization, with category-specific guidance for people, institutions, places, events, periods, titles, and terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers capitalization of proper nouns, first words after colons or in titles, Christian names, governmental departments, Congress, legislative and judiciary bodies, military titles, religious denominations/sects/orders, movements, dynasties, geologic/historical epochs, feast-days, offices, honorifics, divisions, and many other specific categories (pp. 1-21, 33-49).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenated and Compound Words: capitalization and formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on capitalization and formation of compounds and hyphenated words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalization of nouns constituting parts of compounds in titles; special lists for compounds with father/mother/fellow/god/half/like/self/skin/store/etc.; compounds with prefixes (anti-, inter-, intra-, post-, sub-, super-, infra-, supra, ultra, quasi, semi, demi, tri-, bi-, vice-, ex-, elect, general, lieutenant) and rules for omission of common elements indicated by hyphen (pp. 183-214, 186-209).

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of words and hyphenation at line-end
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems and rules governing word division and avoiding undesirable divisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for word division, systems of division (English system), avoidance of division at certain positions (next-to-last line, end of recto), avoid dividing short words or on certain letter combinations (do not divide on soft g or c), and use of hyphen to indicate division (pp. 215-230, 221-227).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and Tabular Work: setting and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules for table design and typesetting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for open vs ruled tables, box-heads, headlines for columns, reading-matter in columns, spacing and setting specimen tables, use of double rules, rules for figures columns, spacing of figure columns, how to set tables to even picas or nonpareils (pp. 240-250, 244-247, 246, 250).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing: rules and standard measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for spacing of text elements and typographic spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines different sizes of spaces (thin, thick, hair, em, en, quad), standard spacing, spacing of divisional signs, numeral spacing at paragraph starts, spacing of headlines, metric symbols, monetary symbols, formulae, short words, and what is considered good spacing (pp. 258-273, 261-264, 269-273).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography technical terms and measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and usage of typographic units and parts of type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines em, en, em-quad, en-quad, quad, pica, nonpareil, minion, pearl, shank, shoulder, kern, face, font, point system, sizes of type, and description of linotype/monotype/setting machines and styles (pp. 251-294, 252-263).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs, Galley-proof, Plate-proof, Page-proof and Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and rules relating to the proofing process and proofreaders' marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions of galley, galley-proof, plate-proof, page-proof, foul proof, foundry-proof; hints to proofreaders and editors; marks of proofreaders; rules for revising and revising stages (pp. 285-294, 105-107, 287-289).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes and Footnotes: numbering and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for footnote formatting and reference indexing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General style for footnotes, numbering/sequence/placement of indices for references to footnotes, numbering of footnotes in linotype matter, exceptions in footnote style, and rules for indices and use of superior figures for reference indices (pp. 230-238, 231-238).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations and Initials: use and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when to abbreviate and punctuation after abbreviations or initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat format (4to, 8vo) not as abbreviation; periods after abbreviations, omission of periods after initials in publication titles, use of small caps for certain abbreviations (P.M.), separation of initials in titles, and list of common abbreviation practices (pp. 61, 123, 52, 219).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations: length, format, and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: How to set quotations: reduced citations, when to run quotations into text or reduce them, and punctuation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for quotations from foreign languages and modern authors, when to reduce extracts, when to run poetry into text vs set separately, italic/quotation mark conventions for quoted material, and punctuation inside/outside quotes (pp. 74-91, 85-87, 59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles, Headings, Headlines, and Running-heads: setting and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for forming, capitalizing, and punctuating different levels of headings and running heads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How to set preface/index quotation marks; omission of periods after headlines/side-heads/legends; 'continued' formatting; setting running-heads and hints for setting; spacing and punctuation for headlines (pp. 73, 125, 279-284, 271-283).

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols and Units (chemical, metric, monetary): treatment and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for dealing with symbols and unit abbreviations and their spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment of metric symbols and system, spacing of metric and monetary symbols, treatment of chemical symbols, abbreviation use for units of measurement, and standards for symbols in text (pp. 111-123, 269-270).

rubrics_metrics.name: Words to be Spelled Out and Spelling conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists and rules for words, phrases, and titles that must be spelled out and accepted spellings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes words to be spelled out (92-105), list of words with multiple spellings, spellings for ages, names of months, titles, United States, decades, Roman/Arabic conventions, and treatment of 'Company'/'Brothers' in firm names (pp. 92-119).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Capitals in Specific Name Classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Category-by-category capitalization rules for specialized name classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalization guidance for dynasties, epochs, events, parks, squares, species, scientific terms, movements, schools, religious orders, nobility, regiments, offices, and many more specific name classes (pp. 2-21, 46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation marks: placement with reference indices and in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for where to print punctuation marks in relation to indices and letters in text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place punctuation marks in same type as preceding character; rules for punctuation placement relative to footnote indices and reference indices in text (pp. 121, 231).
